sites.description: ALPU-MP anti-clone challenge-response bypass. Patches the gate's terminal-failure branch (IRAM 0x16c46, copied to this flash address at boot) so the auth-success path is taken unconditionally.
sites.hook_convention: in-place instruction patch (4 bytes: 20 e9 04 00 -> 03 6c 03 6c at sector offset 0x866) - not a hook/trampoline, a direct edit of the branch encoding
sites.status_evidence: the ALPU-bypass artifacts shipped here document a stock sector backup (sector_030c6000_stock.bin) and a patched sector (sector_030c6000_alpubypass.bin) as real artifacts, implying this was built and applied, not just designed

sites.description: The base live-RAM capture hook every probe variant (MEGAPROBE/AUDIOPROBE/PLLPROBE/CALPROBE/etc.) shares: replaces the stock 'movi r8,0' inside serial_protocol_vframe_command_loop's unknown-sub-id fallthrough with a bsr into a handler at flash 0x030E1000.
sites.hook_convention: 4-byte in-place instruction edit (08 ea 00 00 -> bsr encoding); entry regs documented as r4=buf, r5=serial obj, r8=sub-id, r14=frame; all paths end at the shared transmit site 0x0302a480 with r8=payload length (build_patch.py:bsr_bytes, the capture handler header comment)
sites.status_evidence: build_patch.py asserts the stock bytes at this address are exactly 08 ea 00 00 before patching, verified independently against data/firmware/DM32.00.01.048.bin for this catalogue (matches); every probe variant below chains onto this same hook
sites.source: the live-RAM capture family; see docs/live-ram-capture.md
sites.note: Falls ~38 bytes PAST the corpus's own recorded end of serial_protocol_vframe_command_loop (corpus: 1042 bytes, ending 0x302a456; hook at 0x302a47c) - independently verified as a real corpus coverage gap (the disassembly between those two points decodes cleanly with no halt_baddata-style stop), not a wrong address. Do not 'fix' this address to make it resolve; fix the corpus's function-boundary recovery instead, if this ever gets revisited.

sites.description: Combined live-RAM-capture-family probe handler: flash identity (JEDEC ID, status register, SFDP header), direct 24-bit flash reads via spi_flash_read_mutex_guarded's inlined recipe (no page/mutex indirection), and the stock RAM-seek/read sub-ids, unioned into one patched sector so a single power-cycle flash covers all of them. The LATEST/combined handler occupying this sector - see the other probe entries below, which chain onto the same sector over time.
sites.hook_convention: whole-sector handler (not an in-place edit): unknown sub-ids fall through to stock behaviour via 'movi r8,0 ; jmp r15' - the project's r8-as-result/length, r15-as-return convention for hand-written patch handlers (see tools/README.md's note on why this convention has no corpus-function override: it belongs to patch code, never to stock firmware)
sites.status_evidence: the live-RAM capture notes document real serial port usage against a live radio (PORT=/dev/cu.usbserial-110), a 'Known session limit' discovered empirically (RAM reads died after ~1856 consecutive commands, observed TWICE), and two prior flashing failures that 'cost a battery pull' on 2026-09-30 - all real-hardware-only failure modes, not something QEMU would show

sites.description: Audio-chain MMIO read probe (sub-ids 0x41-0x44: baseband block, prompt-tone FIFO + codec registers, clock registers). Shares the live-RAM capture sector; superseded in-place by later probe variants.
sites.hook_convention: same whole-sector handler convention as megaprobe-handler
sites.status_evidence: 'The probe flashed and connected fine (connected: DP570UV)'; the read-only sub-ids 0x41-0x44 are explicitly called 'known-good'. A separate add-on (beep-probe, sub-id 0x45/0x2c) in the same file failed on hardware twice and was closed - see the beepprobe entry below, catalogued separately since it is a different sub-feature with a different outcome.

sites.description: A 4-byte bsr-shaped overwrite inside the CPS handshake command-dispatch function, found already present on this unit's flash and NOT authored by this project (checked against every backup and build artifact this project has; none created it). Targeted 0x030E1434, which this project's own repeated erase/rewrite cycles of the 0x030E1000 sector had left entirely erased (0xFF) - a dangling reference to a handler that no longer exists. Branching into erased flash during the CPS SYSINFO step caused the radio to hang/reboot, blocking every live-RAM capture-driven operation. REVERTED 2026-09-29 by reflashing sector 0x0302B000 from the verified stock backup; confirmed working (SYSINFO succeeded, full 32KB SRAM dump completed) immediately after. No longer present on the radio as of the revert.
sites.hook_convention: in-place 4-byte bsr-shaped overwrite, same CK803S bsr opcode shape this project's own hook-building code uses, but of unknown/third-party origin
sites.status_evidence: the undocumented-hook notes' 'UPDATE 2026-09-29' section documents the live crash-to-fix sequence and the specific revert action taken
sites.note: CORRECTED 2026-10-06: this doc originally also flagged 0x030C6866 as a second undocumented/third-party diff. That was wrong - 0x030C6866 is this project's own alpu-mp-bypass (see that entry above), misattributed because the 2026-09-29 investigation never cross-referenced the project's own 2026-09-27 ALPU-MP work. Fixed in the source doc directly; this note exists so the correction is visible from this catalogue too.

sites.description: Proof-of-concept UI draw-call overlay hook, installed AFTER the prologue of display_draw_string_gb2312 (not at its entry, 0x03018998 - entry-hooking was tried first and explicitly documented as broken: it clobbers r15 before the function's own push saves it).
sites.hook_convention: 4-byte bsr hook after the function prologue, into a trampoline that re-executes the two displaced stock instructions before running overlay code, guarded by an SRAM re-entrancy flag at 0x18007FE0
sites.status_evidence: 'Not run on hardware. Flashing this requires the full CLAUDE.md safety procedure.' Verified only by booting the patched image under qemu-system-cskyv2 against a emulator-only flash image (flash_overlay.bin), not any hardware backup.

sites.description: Demonstration mod: static ASCII string 'DP570UV' overwritten with 'DM32MOD' (same length, 6 bytes differ) at its single occurrence in the image. No code/hook involved - a pure data-sector edit.
sites.hook_convention: static-data overwrite only; no instruction or branch modified
sites.status_evidence: 'NOT yet flashed to hardware (user's call).' Validated via the mod-validate harness under qemu-cskyv2 (fnverify): pointer table intact, strlen/table lookups through the new string all correct.
